Thank you for the opportunity to provide an update on Loudoun County Public Schools' proposed legislative priorities for the upcoming 2027 Virginia General Assembly session, as well as an overview of our upcoming legislative breakfast. As we prepare for the 2027 General Assembly, LCPS has taken a

deliberate and collaborative approach to identifying the issues we believe are most important to our students, families, educators, and community. Rather than developing a legislative agenda in isolation, we engaged a diverse group of 42 participants from across the school division and the broader community. This group included parents, students, principals, cabinet members, and departmental staff, bringing a wide range of experiences and perspectives to the conversation.

We convened a stakeholder roundtable to create an intentional opportunity for participants to identify emerging challenges share experiences and discuss potential policy solutions and help determine the legislative issues that should be that should receive our attention during this upcoming session the participants engaged in small group discussions focusing on five areas that have been determined uh that we can anticipate a lot of discussion and a lot of

amazing. The result of the proposed agenda is grounded in experiences of the people we serve and inform by, again, a cross-section of our school division and our community. So let me go through

them if I can. At the center of our agenda is the K-12 education funding and equity. Loudoun County continues to be very large and very diversified, and sustainable state investment is essential if we're going to provide every student with the resources and opportunities that they need to be successful.

We will continue to advocate for sustained investment in several critical areas this year, including student mental health and well-being, high-quality and affordable pre-K, English learner education, and intentional technology infrastructure that's going to be necessary to provide a comprehensive and equitable education.

For early childhood education, we support the funding for high-quality pre-K. Expanding access to pre-K gives children an opportunity to develop academic, social, and emotional foundations they need to enter kindergarten and to learn.

For our English learner students, we support increased aid, excuse me, increased funding that recognize the staffing, infrastructure, instructional translation, family engagement, counseling, wraparound supports necessary to meet the needs of a growing and increasingly diverse student population.

We also will continue to emphasize the importance of adequate and sustainable funding for school operations, staffing, infrastructure, and general programs. Ultimately, investment allows local school divisions to manage local resources responsibly while maintaining high-quality educational opportunities for our students.

Let's talk about secondary and post-secondary access, which is going to be a huge issue this year. This is our second major area that we're going to be talking about, particularly career-connected learning and workforce development. We will continue to advocate for increased support for dual enrollment, technical training, career readiness initiatives, and youth pre-apprenticeship opportunities.

These programs give students the opportunity to explore careers, develop technical and employable skills in our industry-recognized credentials, and gain meaningful work-based learning experiences while they are still in high school. We also see tremendous value in strengthening partnerships among schools, colleges, businesses, workforce partners, and community organizations.

The goal is to work with our legislative partners to create clear pathways from high school into registered apprenticeships, post-secondary education, and high-demand careers, while also helping employers develop a strong pipeline of skilled and work-ready talent.

This is an area where education and workforce policy are increasingly interconnected, and we believe Virginia has an opportunity to make strategic investments that benefit both students and the commonwealth's economy. Let's talk about student health, mental health, and well-being.

Again, another issue that is going to be talked about on a large scale this year. LCPS is committed to ensuring that students have access to mental and behavioral health support they need to succeed academically, socially, and quite frankly, personally.

We will advocate for sustainable, recurring funding to expand school-based mental and behavioral health services, strengthen staffing for our school counselors, psychologists, social workers, nurses, behavioral specialists, and other student support professionals.

We also support investments in prevention, early identification and screening, suicide prevention, crisis response, mental health awareness, and professional development for school personnel so that they can, because they're on the front lines, so that they can really take hold of what's going on.

Partnerships are also critical. Schools cannot address issues alone. We need strong partnerships with families, community service boards, health providers, and other community organizations. We also are looking at strengthening Medicaid reimbursement for eligible school-based mental health services and ensuring that services are responsive and accessible to all of our students and families.

That's crucial.
